items.body: A book I've started arguing with in the margins. I don't think he believes his own third chapter, and I've written so in pencil eleven times.
Most productivity systems are just anxiety with a user interface.
items.struck: v2 — all productivity systems are anxiety with a user interface.
items.note: Softened after losing an argument to someone who uses index cards.
items.scar: index cards are not anxiety, they are furniture.

items.body: Every group chat has one person quietly keeping it alive, and it is never the person who talks most.
A napkin diagram I no longer understand. Appears to be either a business model or a seating chart.
Cause of death: the author kept writing “as we shall see.” We did not, in fact, see.
A 1970s cookbook I never cook from → an argument I lost about ritual versus output → I now make coffee badly, on purpose, every morning.
items.note: Three things I thought were unrelated for about nine years.

items.body: Nobody has ever described their own taste accurately. You can only be caught having it.
